verdicts.note: The move to file sector 57 holds up. I modelled the real KZIP load on the six shipped system images (build/os8088-360/-720/-120/os8088.img, small360/720) with blob lengths 13, 14 and 15. The plain head is KZ_HEADSEC=9 sectors in runs of its own (boot2.asm:341-343), and the tail then starts a fresh run at .text+9 (boot2.asm:350-354). Under that model sector 57 sits in a run that crosses a head on every image, whether the head is read cylinder-bound or track-bound. Three things must change. (1) kern_small 360/720 is described wrongly. Its canary is not only 'defeated by the splash', it is INERT, exactly as on kern_big 360/720. The Makefile:2252 +1024 puts kern_small's KSIG at memory 5120 = kernel sector 10, past KZ_HEADSEC 9 (build/smallk/kernel.kz.json headsecs 9), so it lands in the tail. The tail starts at LBA 23+9=32 (head 1, sector 6), its first run is LBA 32..35 on head 1 only, and the canary is LBA 33. The area report's 'both kern_small disks are still correct' (boot.md boot-1) is false. (2) The proposed crosses() fix (start at data+boot2_secs) is still the wrong model. Walking from 23 gives run 23..35, which crosses at 27, so it would still pass small360's inert sector 21. crosses() must split the walk the way the loader does: KZ_HEADSEC from kernel.kz.json in its own runs (track-bound once the second half of this item lands), then the tail restarting at .text+KZ_HEADSEC. The break-on-purpose check (KSIG_OFF back to 4096) must turn small360.img red as well as os8088-360.img. boot-10's 'compute KSIG_OFF from crosses()' inherits the same requirement. (3) Under KZIP the boot-2 half is simpler than 'keep the track bound until SPL_RESIDENT sectors are aboard'. KZ_HEADSEC *is* SPL_RESIDENT and no tick runs during the head loop (boot2.asm:330-343, 361-366), so it reduces to reading the head loop at the track bound and computing the cylinder [b2_runmax] between .head_next and .load_next. That widening must be skipped on the .rerun shortened reload (boot2.asm:525-529), or it undoes the rescue. Fit: no conflict with plans, and the literal still moves as before (Makefile:2242/2252 offsets, boot2.asm:58 equ). Batch A's net .boot2 of about +10 against 4 bytes free (boot.md boot-2) may push kern_big's blob to 14 sectors; 57 still crosses at 14 and 15, but KSIG_OFF's memory literal would then drop by 512.

[dsk_dseg] is 0 at rest: disk.inc:6268 says '[dsk_dseg] is 0 at rest and the CALLER's store during a loud mount', and every fmv_* aim retires through dsk_dest_0 (disk.inc:8577-8583). So a skip of MC_SEG == [dsk_dseg] in mem_shed_one (memory.inc:1418-1438, beside the mem_fatw_dirty skip) takes effect only inside an aimed mount and cannot pin a VIEW cache across the session. That keeps memory.inc's rank argument for MEM_PG_LOW intact, the concern LISTING-HOME-PLAN.md 11.3 raises about leaving the word naming a purgeable claim. Placing the skip at the shed door also covers the harvest-time claimers (ico_need/asc_use) without per-site fixes. kern_big needs nothing here, because compaction is already covered by the MEM_RR_ONE dsk_dseg row (memory.inc:3391). The alternative of raising a mem_pg_fl floor (memory.inc:1399-1412) is coarser, since it would also stop other windows' VIEW caches being shed. The fix should carry the SPEC.md 22.6.3 correction (SPEC.md:53470 'the one claimer ... is asc_use') in the same change, per CLAUDE.md's 'update SPEC before the change'.

Confirmed at the current lines. kernel/vga12.inc:1896-1899 has `or cx,cx / jz vga_b4out / or dx,dx / jz vga_b4out`, short jumps back to the stub at vga12.inc:1714. A short jle has the same 2-byte encoding and the same reach, so the change costs 0 bytes and does not move the layout argument in the stub's comment (vga12.inc:1709-1713). gfx_blitp already carries exactly this guard with the PaccMan rationale (vga12.inc:2867-2870), so the change aligns the two doors rather than inventing a convention. The SDK (apps/os88api.inc:1964-1967) gives no meaning to widths at or above 32768, and no adapter or extended mode comes near that, so treating them as negative refuses nothing legal. The KERN_BIG region walk re-enters with positive fragment sizes only. No synthesis conflicts: systemic.md:482-483 and 533 list the same 0-byte fix. The optional gfx_blit1_x jcxz change costs +2 bytes, as stated.

The direction is right and matches systemic.md ctx-1 (lines 155-166, which drops hm-3's and mem-10's own fixes). As written, though, the fix cannot work. It sends teardown through the window's wm_clreq bit into '.cl_slot ... app_close_win's task-less arm'. app_close_win first calls wm_ask_close (instance.inc:1658), the package's close negotiator, on a dying package. It then refuses any record whose I_STATE is not 1 (instance.inc:1669-1670, 'already dying: re-hide'). inst_task_die's record is already I_STATE 2 (banner, instance.inc:1889-1891), so the posted close would just wm_hide and leak the region. Amend as follows. (a) Post a reap through a UI-task drain of its own, on the inst_launch_post precedent (instance.inc after 2240, drained by ui_task step 3), not wm_clreq. (b) Enter a new label in app_close_win's tail at inst_unwin, then mem_free_rec, desk_drop_x and I_STATE=0 (instance.inc:1721-1734), under gfx_lock and skipping wm_ask_close and the state test. inst_rel_rec and toast_owner_gone stay on the worker, because they are shallow (instance.inc:1930-1932). (c) The worker must task_exit with BX=0 and no release byte, as in the .orphan precedent (instance.inc:2234-2235). Setting I_TASK=0xFF, posting and task_exit must share one IF=0 window, so the UI task can never free a record that a still-live task's exit then releases. (d) SPEC.md 20.6's invariant ('the ONLY code that can free its instance record is the worker's own task_exit', instance.inc banner after 1955) and 11.103.10's 'a Sticky App on its worker arm closes HERE, on that worker' (instance.inc:1945-1947) must be rewritten first. The windowless-record case then needs no special handling, since inst_unwin already skips BX=0 (instance.inc:1912-1914). Expect the bytes at the top of +15..+30.

The mechanism is confirmed: one byte (driver.inc:6132), the 91-tick wait that skips drv_release on timeout (driver.inc:4164-4182), drv_shutdown_x unloading every row in turn (driver.inc:4199-4210), and the whole-image pin (memory.inc:2143). Three things must change. (1) The likelihood is wrong. USBMOUSE.DRV spawns its worker only on the CH375 path, the Book8088's socket. On a PicoMEM 'a PicoMEM's mouse arrives by interrupt: no chip to poll, so no worker' (drivers/usbmouse/usbmouse.asm:140-142). So it is 'every Book8088/CH375 USB-mouse machine', not 'every PicoMEM USB-mouse machine'. (2) This is NO-PINNING-PLAN.md K1b (docs/plans/NO-PINNING-PLAN.md:177, 260): a per-row worker count in drv_tab, bumped at spawn and exit, which .drvimg tests. That row already records 'Deferred; its condition is now met' and cites drivers-1. Land BR-5 as K1b, update or close that plan row in the same commit, and reconcile the byte estimate: the plan says ~45 + DRV_MAX .bss, BR-5 says ~25 .cold + 11 .bss (DRV_MAX = 9+DRV_VX+DRV_PX on kern_big, driver.inc:80). (3) Unpublishing the class on timeout fits the existing 'leak, never a free under a live CS' rule (driver.inc:4178-4181), since the image stays claimed. With per-row counts, though, the timeout only happens for a buggy driver, so treat it as a secondary part of the fix, not the cure for the 5-second stall. No other synthesis or ABI-BREAK-LIST row conflicts.

The 'take' half fits LAST-DROP-PERF 7.4. Its first flip condition, 'A bigger round', is this case. The 'delete every losing arm' half conflicts with an owner decision and with kern_mega.

(1) docs/plans/khp1/LOG.md L.3 quotes the owner: "The temporary branch will not live long enough to cherry pick off of ... we could make them a knob for them, with them off for now." The 1bpp items are knobs so that they outlive kernel-hotpaths. kernel.asm:276-277 says the same: "kept as knobs so they outlive the branch". The LAST-DROP-PERF banner (lines 4-9) also defines the register as "deferred indefinitely ... no row is owed". Deleting the MONOSCROLL, MONOPAT or MONORECT arms (rows 12/14/16) reverses that decision. Change: an arm is deleted only with the owner's word. If it is deleted, it becomes a patch under docs/plans/khp1/patches/, the owner's other option ("put them into a file alongside the perf doc") and disk-4's precedent. It must not just disappear.

(2) kern_mega defines KHP_FRAME, KHP_FPG, KHP_RAISEOL and KHP_VGABLITP (kernel.asm:297-303). Refusing row 11 (FRAME), or rows 7 and 9, on kern_big cannot delete their arms. Either kern_mega changes (the bytes line says 'kern_mega 0'), or the %ifdef becomes a KERN_MEGA/else split, which keeps both arms living. The sentence 'both arms stop living in wm.inc and softgfx.inc' must exempt every row kern_mega carries.

(3) The owner's bar for the khp1 round was "around 100b" (LOG.md L). The take set is +104 everywhere and +286 on the VGA gauge, so present it as a request for a bigger round, not as the review's default. phase1 already lists the .vga rows (+182) first in its drop order.

Minor: the KHP block is kernel.asm:252-307, not 243-297.

verdicts.note:
histsys-3, dw-16, dw-17 and dw-20 fit. Two problems:

(1) dw-15 overstates what it saves, and there is a cheaper, narrower shape. gfx_unlock still flushes once per user operation. A single delete, rmdir, truncate or save-replace therefore spends the same two FAT writes whether it flushes in dskw_relold (diskw.inc:963-974) or at gfx_unlock. The '~0.8 s each' saving exists only when several frees happen under one lock: rmtree's 50 files, a multi-select delete, a copy that replaces. Deferring to gfx_unlock gives up dskw_relold's stated invariant, "a commit point leaves the window CLEAN (dsk_fatw_park relies on it - dirt carried across a media change lands on the NEXT disk's FAT)" (diskw.inc:965-968), on every path, to win on a few. Change: confine the lazy state to the multi-op brackets, i.e. inside dskw_rmtree and between OSAPI_BATCH_BEGIN/END (os88api.inc:6086-6087). The area finding (diskwrite.md:303) names BATCH_END as a flush point, and the synthesis dropped it. The commit-point invariant then holds everywhere else, dsk_fatw_park's exposure does not widen, and the dependency on BR-133/dw-5 shrinks to the bracket.

(2) dw-14 contradicts a stated SPEC non-goal. SPEC.md:34844-34848 says "What this deliberately does not do ... no attempt to defragment while writing: chains are allocated first-fit from the rover". Per CLAUDE.md, SPEC changes before the code, so dw-14 must first rewrite that paragraph (18.4) as a dated decision. The paragraph is in the Files list but not called out.

The dw-5-first dependency stands.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: kern_big about +105 .cold as given; dw-15 saves int 13h calls only for multi-op sequences (rmtree, batch), 0 calls for a single delete/replace

verdicts.note:
Most items fit and none is already done:
- engsys-15 matches CLAUDE.md's soak rule and os88test.py:1319, which refuses only an empty -k, so '*' really does pass.
- t_mirror names no kerndos file.
- os88.h is outside the lock.

One overlap needs resolving. engsys-3 (have t_mirror read SPEC's fenced nasm, 'or generate §3 and §15.1 between markers') runs into WP24. WP24's own rule is 'every copy is either generated or deleted' (phase1 WP24), and its engsys-4 rewrites SPEC §1-§4 and §15-§17 as current front matter. A t_mirror gate over §3's hand copy, built just before WP24 rewrites §3, is spent twice. Change: WP10 fixes the four wrong values now (KERNEL_SEG, STK0_SIZE, KERN_BUDGET, DSV_SIZE) and adds the general SPEC-fence check for the other ~178 'NAME equ N' lines. §3 and §15.1 are generated or deleted inside WP24's rewrite. The heading-drift check (engsys-2) must land before WP24's engsys-18 SPEC split, as WP24 says. It must then also resolve citations into the new <PKG>-SPEC.md files, or the split blinds it.

engsys-15's ~90% threshold is new policy and stays the owner's call, as written.

Three changes.

(1) mem-17 has no free 'header bit'. SPEC.md 20.2's header row (about SPEC.md:44208) and os88api.inc:4233-4246 assign all eight flags bits: 0 ICON, 1 ASSOC, 2 PARTS, 3-4 compression (os88pkg.py:200 refuses them from source), 5 GLYPH, 6 DESK, 7 STIK. The bit must live elsewhere, and the claim 'old kernels just run those packages pinned' must be re-proved for wherever it goes. The nearest candidate is the high bit of LD_H_CLASS (byte 15). Old loaders do not validate that byte, and the consumer maps an out-of-range index to the largest stack class (loader.inc:114-126). That is safe, but on an old kernel the package then loses its declared worker class. Anything else grows the header, which means a PKG_FMT bump under §20.2.0.1. State the chosen field and that cost.

(2) hm-11's savings are total op_* spans (histmem.md:355-362), not the droppable part. browser, pixel and video all declare OP_LAZY rows (browser.asm:14368, pixel.asm:4046-4054, video.asm). For those, op_fetch (os88partsbody.inc:1934) keeps op_read, op_row, op_clbget, op_lazyp, op_zrpara, op_ata, op_asop and op_say resident for life; only op_load, op_size, op_claim, op_xload and op_unpack's load-time half can go. Re-measure the droppable span per package before quoting -0.8..-1.5KB. The KEEP-form REHOME it relies on is the form ABI-BREAK-LIST R1 keeps (ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:147), so that part fits.

(3) text-15 does not 'retire the case-6 registry rows'. The bold is kern_big-only (+35..45). Word, Texpad, Frotz and cword still run on kern_small and on older kernels, so they keep their overstrike path. Their transparent call sites stay, and so do their tests/textsites.txt rows. Either add the bold on kern_small too, against its 64KB budget, or say the rows stay until the packages can refuse elsewhere (WP9's OS88_NEED).

The core of WP4 (histsys-7) is sound, and it agrees with systemic.md:941-948 and with flagday D1/D4 (flagday.md:171, 264). Four things should change.
(1) A cheaper form of the length test. The ~14 non-sound readers already go through drv_cls_svc_x (driver.inc:1923; callers include assoc.inc:1093, desk.inc:1774, disk.inc:1605/2193, fsx.inc:2019, hiber.inc:1685, ctrl.inc:2855). So do not put a DRV_H_DSV length test at each read site. Turn that accessor into a cell fetch that answers 0 for any cell past the table: one test, and flagday D4's table floor later deletes exactly one test. Also, publish skips EMS, so EMS keeps no copy (driver.inc:4038-4048). The only shipped driver with a short table that reaches an in-place read is HDD.DRV.
(2) drivers-10's +~100 in the blob is not a committed saving. phase1.md:127's own ledger has the blob 4 bytes free and wanting +162..172 against WP6's -41/-54. Make drivers-10 conditional on the owner's 14th-sector decision or on boot-17, and count only bytes-8's -25 kern_big / -10 kern_small (bytes.md:703) as firm.

The substance fits. No owner decision or plan refuses an int 0 handler (no hits in docs/plans, FIELD-NOTES or git -S). The kernel's own 'a halted machine is a bug report' (sched.inc:2601-2612) and SPEC 88.9's ADI story (SPEC.md ~166110) both argue for it. int0sweep traps the INT instruction itself, with a debugger 'int' breakpoint (tests/int0sweep.py), so a kernel handler does not blind it. Three amendments:
(1) This is double-booked. The same fixes are BR-8 and BR-9 in bugs.md:160-180, priced again in bugs.md:1055 (+30). Name one owner, so the +30 stubs and the wm-2 bytes are counted once. The bug pass also carries the cheaper non-growing alternative, 'cmp ax,MAX_WIN*WIN_SIZE / jae' (+5).
(2) W_IDX makes kern_big's WIN_SIZE odd (74 -> 75, wm.inc:128). Every other record's word fields would then be odd-addressed on the 16-bit-bus machines kern_big also runs on, which works against the -80-clock rationale there. kern_small is already odd (65) and is fine on an 8088. Pad to 76 on kern_big (+12 .bss more), or state the trade. 'Outside wm_create's zero run' means shortening the run that zeroes W_MENUS..WIN_SIZE (wm.inc:97-99) to stop before W_IDX.
(3) The BOOT_MARK knob's mark_hook (kernel.asm:7720-7752) is the existing stub precedent to reuse. But its vector list includes 5 (mark_fvec), and WP8 rightly forbids hooking 5, so reuse the shape and not the list.

verdicts.note:
WP9 conflicts with the review's own reconciliation. Systemic theme 9 (systemic.md:870-884) and flagday A4 (flagday.md:295) both say, per gfr-5, to publish a LEVEL at 0060:0006 ('dw OS88_API_LEVEL'), not osapi_table_end. The reason is that T5/bytes-1 takes the rare cells out of the table, after which a table end no longer describes the API. Packages built with WP9's 'OS88_NEED cell' / 'cmp word [es:6], cell+1' would then be compiled against a meaning that changes. Make the word a level, give OS88_NEED a level argument, and use one numbering (The Wire's WIRE_CELL_LEVELS, tools/os88wire.py:120-131) for both the word and header byte 31.
The caveat can be closed. The mouse-instrument word left 0x0006 in 2ae27476 (#112, 2026-08-24). PKG_FMT 10 arrived in b47de145 (#252, 2026-10-14), and that tree's kernel.asm already reads '0x06..0x07 stay free'. So every PKG_FMT-10 kernel reads 0 there.
New hazard: byte 31 is the NUL terminator of a 15-character name.
- The kernel is safe: inst_set_name_x takes at most 15 characters (SPEC.md:68065).
- os88pkg.py:122-125 would fail such a package.
- os88disk.py:289-293 would fail it as 'non-printable' (any level below 0x20).
- os88pkgsize.py:41 and os88rate.py:150 would misread the name.
Cap names at 14 characters whenever byte 31 is set (no in-tree name is longer than 13: 'Desk Calendar', 'Pixelstein 3D'), or bound every host reader at 15.

The core move (inst_task_die posts teardown to the UI task) fits. It is the same post-to-UI shape the kernel already uses six times. kern_mega's mega_fkill already does owner-died release and posted teardown, and nothing on record refuses it. Five things must change.
(1) dw-4's retail refusal conflicts with T5 and with an owner ruling. T1 ships `cmp byte [sch_cur],0` in the file cells' N-stub as +9 resident. T5's APICHK=1 puts the same check ("file cells check [sch_cur]=0") in a knob build at 0 shipped bytes. The owner's ruling is "packages are trusted ... a check that exists only to defend the kernel from its caller is not a reason to keep a byte" (docs/plans/LAST-DROP-BYTES.md:1135-1140, SPEC.md:73063). Pick one: either APICHK only, or put dw-4 to the owner as a named exception (a cross-linked FAT survives the reboot that ends every other package fault). Do not count it in both themes.
(2) The bytes for ctx-2 are the uncorrected ones. The verifier corrected them to +12 .text kern_big/kern_small and about -24 .mega (data/gap-context-lock-model.json ctx-2 verify_note), not +9/-13. ctx-1's verified estimate is +16..+26, not +12..+30.
(3) "hm-3 and mem-10's own fixes are then unnecessary" contradicts phase1 WP2 (synth/phase1.md:244-256, 277, 294). WP2 calls mem-10's deferred drop "the pin's foundation" and prices it +8..12. Say instead that T1 provides the post-to-UI mechanism WP2 step (1) needs (phase1.md:315-317, "whichever lands first"). mem-10's second half, the "frame standing in this image" fact for the module pin, is still needed. A one-line assert that mod_drop runs on task 0 should replace the deleted arm.
(4) Two specs pick different mechanisms. ctx-1 adds a new `.bss` word [inst_reap]. BR-4 (synth/bugs.md:126) reuses the existing wm_clreq bit, plus a reap byte only for a windowless record. Choose BR-4's: it adds no new drain loop.
(5) SPEC.md:22809 currently binds the opposite ("`inst_task_die`, under the gfx lock | a Sticky App on its worker arm ... whose record is freed on that worker"). Per CLAUDE.md, SPEC.md is updated before the change. Leave NO-PINNING-PLAN's built K8 sch_cur gate (+14) in place: it still covers driver verbs and rule-7 violators (docs/plans/NO-PINNING-PLAN.md:398).

The now-half fits. No owner decision refuses an int 0 handler. tests/int0sweep.py arms an interrupt-type breakpoint (`{"type": "int", "addr": 0}`, int0sweep.py:67), so a kernel stub does not blind it. Windowed DOS already banks IVT 00h (apps/dos/dosw.inc:89,111). Two fit problems.
(1) The flag-day rule "AX=1 means 'not on this kernel' everywhere" collides with an existing code. FERR_NODISK is 1 and means "no mounted data disk" (apps/os88api.inc:4009), a real file condition the file cells return today. The claim, and flagday R9 (synth/flagday.md:251), count FERR_NODISK as "already answering 1", but with the other meaning. Under R9, a file-cell caller seeing CF=1, AX=1 cannot tell "insert a disk" from "cell absent". Per abi-9, kern_small's file cells answer FERR_PROT (8) for "not here". Fix: either exempt families that already own 1 (FERR), so the rule reads "AX=1 = not here in any cell with no family code, or that names XREFUSE", which the same item's now-sentence already says. Or renumber FERR_NODISK, which is a PKG_FMT event the item says it is avoiding. Drop "everywhere".
(2) Taking int 6 on a 286+ makes vector 06h load-bearing, and windowed DOS does not bank it. dvw_runs (apps/dos/dosw.inc:110-116) banks only 00h, 08h-0Fh and 10h-3Fh. A windowed DOS program that hooks int 6 (the usual invalid-opcode CPU probe) would replace the kernel's handler for every task and leave it pointing into the freed world. Add a 06h run (+6 bytes of DOS.O88 table) in the same change, or install int 6 only where the fault stays fatal and say so.

The two halves fit differently.
The hostile-FILE half fits the project's threat model and stands. That is loader-1/loader-3's prefix bound in ld_check_hdr (a HIGH), dw-1's FileSize clamp at dsk_get_dir, sysmisc-2's CFG domain column, gfx-1's 0-byte jz->jle and wm-2's W_IDX. W_IDX is justified on speed (about -80 clocks a call, net +4/-2) and removes a div; WIN_SIZE is unpublished, with only the tools/os88geom.py mirror.
The package-pointer half conflicts with a standing owner ruling. The ruling: "packages are trusted — this is real mode, and a package that misbehaves takes the machine down whatever the kernel refuses — so a check that exists only to defend the kernel from its caller is not a reason to keep a byte" (docs/plans/LAST-DROP-BYTES.md:1135-1140, applied at SPEC.md:73063 and :73663). The affected fences: histsys-11's wm_isrec at WM_WAKE/MEMC_POST (the SDK says "BX is trusted", apps/os88api.inc:1733), loader-4's entry-BX check (its own verify note: "a package is trusted code") and hm-2. hm-2 additionally reverses an explicit SPEC decision: freeing or regrowing one's own region with `mov dx, cs` is "a package shooting itself and not a thing the kernel undertakes to prevent" (SPEC.md:120494-120495). Its verifier lowered it to low and called it "a policy reversal" (data/histmem.json hm-2).
Amend: move histsys-11, loader-4 and hm-2 into the APICHK=1 build the item already proposes, which is exactly the trust-respecting shape. Or put each to the owner as an exception with its own argument. Do not list them as retail "fences at the funnels". hm-14 can stay retail if it is argued as forward compatibility (an older kernel answering a newer SDK's verb as AVAIL), which belongs with T9, not as defence. The resident total drops by about 20..38 accordingly.

The direction fits and is not on ABI-BREAK-LIST. It also agrees with flagday A4 (synth/flagday.md:295). Three fit problems.
(1) The syntheses disagree on what goes at 0060:0006. phase1 WP9 publishes `dw osapi_table_end` there and keys OS88_NEED on a cell address (synth/phase1.md:714-720, :154). systemic and flagday publish a LEVEL, because flagday T5 takes rare cells out of the table. Fix phase1 WP9 to the level so one design goes forward.
(2) Byte 31 is not free padding: it is the NUL of a 15-character name. tools/os88pkg.py:119-124 accepts names up to 15 chars and fails any non-NUL byte after the terminator. So os88pkg must cap names at 14 and exempt byte 31 from the after-terminator check. That costs nothing today: the longest name in build/*.bin is 13 characters ("Desk Calendar", "Pixelstein 3D"). The kernel copy is already safe, since inst_set_name_x takes at most 15 chars (kernel/instance.inc:1229, 1235). Host readers that split [16:32] on NUL would read the level into a 15-character name: tools/os88disk.py:289, os88drv.py:196, os88pkgsize.py:41, tests/heapscrl.py:276, tests/tmload.py:151, tests/rehome.py:172. So the 14-char cap is the cheap answer, not changing every reader.
(3) The PM-clean bit at +15 bit 5 needs the new kernel to change `and bx, 0x3F` to 0x1F (kernel/instance.inc:2107). Otherwise a clean package gets an out-of-range class and silently launches with the largest stack. flagday.md:74-77 and L7 say this; the systemic item drops it. mc-19 is still (unchecked).

The lifetimes-by-count parts fit. drivers-1 per-row worker counts are now due: NO-PINNING K1b deferred them "until a second driver spawns a worker", and USBMOUSE.DRV now does. drivers-2's bounded wait and shell-1's IF_LIB fit too, as do the AT rung (a second instance of the .vga run-time door, which needs its tests/atrefs.txt registry per CLAUDE.md) and text-7, which is flagged as the owner's call. Three fit problems.
(1) Preloading FILECP/FDLG into purgeable claims answers ONDEMAND-PLAN 1.2's objection only while nothing sheds them. Under pressure the purge brings the objection back word for word: "The chooser cannot be the thing that costs you the disk you are choosing on" (docs/plans/completed/ONDEMAND-PLAN.md:119-131). A kern_big Save As would then answer "Needs Sys Disk A:" with the apps disk in the drive. The item and phase1 WP2 rate this risk high but give it no policy. Amend: rank these two images to shed last, or only for a package LAUNCH's claim (which is user-initiated, with the refusal visible at that moment), never for a running package's growth. Add the row phase1 already wants ("shed FILECP under pressure, then Save As").
(2) KBMOUSE "loaded on the first claimed key" needs a system-disk read at exactly the moment a mouseless desktop needs its only pointer. That fails CLAUDE.md's module test ("the system disk is already required ... or can be required without interrupting what the user was doing"). input-12's verifier calls it "a judgement for the owner, not a defect". Cheaper and inside the rule: load the module in the boot read (bytes-3's KERNEL.SYS preload shape, or at mouse detection while A: is the boot disk), and drop it when [mou_ptr] is set. The -300..-380 then holds on every machine with a mouse, and no keypress ever waits on the disk.
(3) This item folds mem-10 "into theme 1" while also listing "mem-10's pin" under WP2. Reconcile the two the same way as T1 item (3): T1 supplies the post, and WP2 still builds the frame-standing count.

The direction holds: no owner refusal is on record against package purgeable claims, and HANDOFF-APPS-SHARED.md:153 lists the purgeable claim as wanted. Four things need to change.
(1) The kern_mega arm is unpriced, and it contradicts a recorded decision. REALDMG-HIGHCACHE-PLAN.md:86 says of MC1: "A package's claim is not a cache and is not shed." On kern_mega package claims are LDT selectors that are rebased, not proc-notified (memory.inc:2995-2998), so a purge with DX=0 also needs the selector invalidated. Otherwise a stale selector reaches a reused block. State one of two things: kern_mega refuses MEMP_PURGEABLE as kern_small does, or the purge frees the selector and the MC1 line is amended.
(2) MC_DMA bit 13 is documented today as part of the head. memory.inc:89 says "Bits 0-13 are the ... HEAD" and MC_DMA_HEAD equ 0x3FFF (memory.inc:169). The change must narrow the mask to 0x1FFF and rewrite that contract comment in the same diff.
(3) The parts init-drop (hm-11) is routed "through OSAPI_PKG_REHOME's KEEP form". That cell is one of the bare refusals on kern_small (ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:127, osapi_pkg_rehome_x). On the 128KB machine, where the KB matter most, the drop must go through OSAPI_MEM_P MEMP_REGROW's shrink (path 1), which is hm-11's own alternative. Say so per kernel. The KEEP form keeps "every part after it" (os88api.inc:1498-1503), so the dropped body must sit at the carve's tail with the bss chain moved below it (OP_BSS_AT).
(4) A shared allocator in apps/os88lmem.inc reaches WIN16 (asm, apps/win16/w16mem.inc), Sheet and DOS, but not WEAVE (wgrid.c, C). The C toolchain cannot %include an asm include, and WEAVE-SPEC 1.2 requires source sharing. Either say three packages, or add a C twin or a thunk.
mem-17's header bit must rewrite CLAUDE.md's OS88_REGION_MOVABLE rule, t_movable and tests/movable.txt in the same diff. That is not a conflict. Handles staying recorded (gfr-4) is consistent with R2-6.

The flag-day door is consistent with the ABI list. It keeps T1 as the fallback, and SPEC.md 20.8 rule 4 still holds because the index refuses (ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:127). The owner declined both smaller forms: T1 ("an ABI break on main", HANDOFF-KERNEL-SIZE-P14 4) and K17-1 ("refused once", ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:284). So T5 must be presented as the owner's flag-day decision at about twice the cycle price, not as a default.
The 'rehearse now' half fails the fit lens as written, for two reasons.
(a) The census is stale. KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.md:8-11, as of 2026-11-08, counts 45 shim bodies and 23 zero-byte aliases (21 are `cw_X equ apic_X`), not 70 shims. An alias has no bytes to save. 45 x (4 - 2) is about -90 of table, and the rehearsal alone pays for the door body (~+45, gfr-1) until T5 shares it. That leaves about -45 .text plus -2 at each site in .cold or a module, not ~-140.
(b) It is not package-free or ABI-free. The door makes kernel-private dispatch depend on an IVT vector, which today's far-call table never does. apps/dos exchanges IVT runs 00h, 08h-0Fh and 10h-3Fh while a windowed program runs (apps/dos/dosw.inc:89-93, dvw_xflip :160-170). Full-screen DOS banks all 512 words (dos.asm:2956-2961). DOS programs write IVT entries routinely. So the vector must be chosen outside those runs, and apps/dos, a shipped package, must refuse or virtualise writes to it in the same change. gfr-1 item 3 raises this only for T5. Otherwise a windowed program that writes the vector kills the desktop's module calls. Theme 2's single IVT owner should own that vector.
The class table also needs a correction. The handler words are interleaved with contract-readable fields (kernel/wm.inc: W_PAINT 12, W_ONKEY 14, W_ONCLICK 16, W_DISP/W_SEG 20-22, W_ONSIZE..W_ONTIMER 24-30, W_TIMER 32, then W_SIDE's W_MINW/W_ZOOMR/W_NATR). The -216 .bss record shrink therefore moves offsets that packages may read (gfr-4: the record is readable by contract, os88api.inc:4188). "Breaks templates and setters but no data access" is wrong unless the vacated words stay as holes. Take abi-7's W_* reader census first.

Three fit problems.
(1) Drawing the cursor after the EOI breaks a written invariant, and the +30..40 does not pay for it. kernel/mouse.inc:357-361 says mou_isr "NEEDS NO RE-ENTRANCY GUARD ... runs with IF=0 from the CPU's own gate to the iret and never stis (SPEC.md 7/9)". Its private-stack entry is an unconditional `mov [cs:x],sp / mov sp,imm16` (:363-366). With `sti` before the redraw, the next IRQ3 or IRQ4 re-enters, overwrites the saved-SP slot and resets SP onto the live outer frame. The change must add a register-free busy test before the swap (`cmp byte [cs:busy],0` needs no register). It must size the private stack for one nested decode beyond today's 54-byte planar depth (:352-355), and reword SPEC 7/9.
isr-7's own cheaper first answer should come before the structural one: a documented ceiling, with the lease defaulted to 2400 on a UART the probe calls an 8250 (WireFleet already asks for that). The structural change follows only if the measurement demands it.
(2) The Record bullet (isr-15, "BIOS mutex in place of sch_lock across int 13h ... only if SB underruns are reported") contradicts T3, which releases sch_lock across the UI task's int 13h "now, after one measurement". It is the same mechanism: ctx-3's disk-owner byte is isr-15's mutex scoped to dsk_xfer. Remove isr-15 from this theme's Record and carry its caveat into T3: every "nothing else runs" invariant must be re-proved, for example the gate at mouse.inc:4232.
(3) input-2's rule (refuse a switch while a non-IRQ0 line is in service) should be ordered before T3's release, because the release widens the windows in which a parked int 09h can be switched away from. Everything else (IMR shadow, IVT scan, OSAPI_IRQ as the owner's call, L3 at the flag day) is consistent with ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:178.

task_wake fits. T_FLAGS bit 1 is free: only TF_SERVICE = bit 0 is defined (kernel/sched.inc:70-75), and task_spawn's word store clears it (:1027-1031). The 'disk wait that freezes nothing' needs three changes.
(1) Resolve the contradiction with T2's Record line (isr-15 kept as record "only if SB underruns are reported"). This theme lists isr-15 as a source and makes the release a now item. One home, with isr-15's re-prove-every-invariant caveat.
(2) A precondition is missing that ctx-3's 'what holds already' does not cover. Windowed DOS exchanges IVT 08h-0Fh (IRQ6's 0Eh included) and 10h-3Fh (13h and 15h included) whenever its worker runs (apps/dos/dosw.inc:89-93; dvw_xflip :160-170; 0Ah-0Fh are "ITS while it runs"). ctx-3 cites only dosw.inc:17's refusing int 13h. With sch_lock released across the UI task's floppy int 13h (now kernel/disk.inc:1470), a tick can switch into a DVW worker mid-transfer. The floppy completion IRQ6 then vectors through the program's 0Eh. On an AT the proposed int 15h AH=90h/91h hook is likewise the program's vector during its slice. Fix: keep the lock while any DVW world can be swapped in, or exclude 0Eh and 15h from the exchange and prove it.
(3) The claim names only ctx-3 as the prerequisite. The synthesis's own 'Ordering across themes' item 1 also puts ctx-1 (teardown on the UI task) before this release. State both, and price it at ctx-3's +33..38 resident, not +16..40.
The file-layer items do not collide with a recorded decision. SPEC's "the kernel does not grow a directory (§18.5)" (SPEC.md:133903, 134407) is stated as a fact, not a refusal, so dw-12 must also edit those lines.

The direction (one source per fact, generators, AGENTS.md generated) fits CLAUDE.md:3-5 and the abi.lock and os88index precedent, but three things must change.
(1) The headline evidence is already fixed on this tree. Commit 14428309 ("Docs and comments brought into line with the code") applied 946 of the review's doc fixes. SPEC.md:4058 now reads KERNEL_SEG equ 0x0060 and :4069 STK0_SIZE 512, and no `§46 rule`/greying citations of §46 remain. So "SPEC.md 3 has KERNEL_SEG 0x0800" and "six citations of 46" should be cited as past instances that show the need for a gate, not as live defects. The "956 doc fixes / comment-discipline sweep" (WP25) is mostly done. What is left is the recurrence gate, not the sweep.
(2) engsys-2's heading-drift check reads {number: title} at `git merge-base HEAD origin/elendilon` from checkdocs, which runs in every make. That conflicts with fork rule 1: on a shallow clone, merge-base returns a confidently wrong base without failing. It also conflicts with rule 7 and upstream: jggonz/os8088 has no elendilon branch, and a release tree may have no git. Use a committed heading lock that is updated deliberately with a reason, as tools/abi.lock.json is, instead.
(3) AGENTS.md generation is still needed. `diff` past the headers is still 705 lines today, so engsys-10 stands.
The per-package SPEC split keeping its numbers matches the WEAVE-SPEC and ARCADE-SPEC precedent. Admission by declaration does not conflict with docs/WRITING-TESTS.md.

The withdrawal survives as a flag-day row, but its correctness argument and part of its bytes need the kernel's own internal callers converted too, and those are a no-bump job (Phase 1). (1) md-16 is not a package door. kerndos/kdshim.inc:409-416 is kern_dos's private mem_claim_x, reached from kerndos/kdgate.inc:97 and from shared kernel code. Withdrawing the six OSAPI cells does not touch it. (2) Inside the kernel the KB entries stay after C1 unless their callers move: mem_claim_x at kernel/disk.inc:9674, kernel/files.inc:1306 and :6071, kernel/memory.inc:6259; mem_regrow at disk.inc:9922 and files.inc:1821; mem_avail_lvl_x at disk.inc:5990/7508 and memory.inc:5354/5790. So the shifts that carried the bug (memory.inc:860-868, 927-929, 4562-4565) do not disappear with the cells. Also, kern_mega's pool counts in KB: mem_claimp_x converts paragraphs to KB at memory.inc:1025-1033. So 'the paragraph door has no shift' holds only once the internal callers move, and a shift stays in the pool arm regardless. (3) The bug itself is already fixed for 0 to +3 bytes by bugs.md BR-105 (synth/bugs.md:888). Amend: (a) count three package-reachable doors, not four, and drop md-16 or label it as kern_dos-internal; (b) state that the ~10-14 bytes of 'KB shifts at the doors' come only after the internal callers move to mem_claimp_x/the paragraph regrow, which is kernel-private and can land now; (c) keep the -35 to -55 figure explicitly conditional on T5. T5 is a re-proposal of a renumber the owner has declined once before (ABI-BREAK-LIST K17-1, line 284), so quote the non-T5 figure (~-50 to -70, ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:134) next to it. I checked that all six cells are rare kinds (kernel.asm:2840-2883, 3804-3815: RCXCELL/RCSLOT), so 12 bytes under T5 is right. This does not conflict with HEAP-GRANULARITY-PLAN 3.3, which kept the KB doors with no bump (C1 is the bump that plan deferred), and nothing similar is in flight in docs/plans/.

The premise is wrong, and the floor needs no flag day. (1) HDD.DRV and EMS.DRV do not declare short tables. hdd.asm:1542-1573 lists all 18 cells, DSV_CAPS through DSV_PKGCALL, which is 36 bytes = DSV_SIZE (os88drv.inc:419). ems.asm:485-487 defines em_svc_end = em_door+2 = DSV_PKGCALL+2 = 36, with the comment '(OS88_DRIVER's +15 table length: DSV_SIZE)'. EMS also has no table copy at all: driver.inc:4040-4048 jumps straight to .owner and says 'Its table is always full length'. Every other driver takes OS88_DRIVER's default length, DSV_SIZE (os88drv.inc:772). (2) DSV_SIZE last changed on 2026-09-08 (2ce1e37b) and FSV_SIZE on 2026-08-17. DRV_VER has moved twice since: 11 in b47de145 on 2026-10-14, 12 in d323a9a6 on 2026-11-02. So every driver the DRV_VER-12 equality test admits already carries full 36-byte DSV and 30-byte FSV tables. The floor already holds, by the same argument N1 makes (ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:160). Writing it down is a contract clarification (an abilock --update with no bump) plus a build-time %error in OS88_DRIVER when %4 < the floor. histsys-7 can then read in place below the floor with no length tests today. (3) 'drv_publish's zero-fill and clamp go' contradicts the row's own 'table growth still needs no bump'. The clamp (driver.inc:4073-4076) is what keeps a longer table from a newer SDK out of an older kernel's copy area. The zero-fill comes back as soon as DSV_SIZE grows past the floor. So the -15 to -25 is at best temporary and partly wrong. Amend: (a) move D4 to Phase 1 next to N1 as 'floor = today's DSV_SIZE/FSV_SIZE at DRV_VER 12'; (b) drop the HDD/EMS padding line; (c) keep the clamp; (d) restate the bytes as histsys-7's length tests avoided below the floor. 'D1 and drivers-9 moot under histsys-7' still stands.

The design is sound, but it has to be reconciled with phase1 and it leaves out an IMR owner. (1) phase1.md:174 (WP22) and :2518 recommend the IMR shadow alone now and the OSAPI_IRQ cell at the flag day. D8 says 'append the cell now (owner's call)'. systemic.md:274-277 sides with D8, and bugs.md:426-427 puts the cell at the flag day. Pick one wording across the syntheses: shadow plus drivers-6's release-time IVT scan (+25 .cold) in Phase 1; the cell either as an owner's-call append or at the flag day. Do not leave the bundle and Phase 1 disagreeing. (2) DOS.O88 is missing from the affected list, though isr-13 itself names it as an owner. Full-screen DOS snapshots and wholesale-restores port 21h/A1h (apps/dos/dos.asm:2989-2992, 3015-3022). Windowed DOS saves and selectively restores 21h (apps/dos/dosw.inc:848-850, 1043-1046). A DOS program inside either writes the PIC directly. A kernel IMR shadow with per-owner bits goes stale across those brackets, and DOS's restore can clobber a bit set through the shadow during a windowed run. D8 must either re-sync the shadow from port 21h after a DOS bracket, or route DOS's restore through the cell. (3) 'Mandatory at DRV_VER 14' binds drivers only. DOS.O88 and os88spk packages still write vectors and the mask, so 'the kernel owns the IVT and IMR' needs a stated package carve-out or a PKG_FMT clause. Without one, deleting the post-detach scan is safe only for driver-held lines. The bytes and the SOUND.DRV -60 are left as estimated.

Making AX=1 universal collides with families that already use 1 for something else, so it is not 'about nothing' and not free of renumbering. EMSE_ROOM equ 1 (apps/os88api.inc:3688) is a real refusal returned through OSAPI_DRV_CALL to the EMS class (drivers/ems/ems.asm:344), and tests/emstest/emstest.asm:15 asserts it. If DRV_CALL's no-driver answer moves from AX=0 (driver.inc:6655-6659) to 1, then on that same cell 'no EMS driver' and 'no run of pages that long' become the same answer. DRVE_DISK equ 1 (driver.inc:274), LD_EDISK equ 1 (loader.inc:45) and FERR_NODISK equ 1 ('no mounted volume', diskw.inc:62) also hold 1 with their own meaning. 'Families start at 2' therefore means renumbering EMSE/DRVE/LD and FERR_NODISK, which is the renumbered error space the row says it avoids, with PKG_FMT and DRV_VER bumps for EMSE. A simpler shape fits better: AX=0 with CF=1 is unused in every family, because 0 means OK in FERR, DRVE and LD, and DRV_CALL already uses it. Either make 0 the universal 'not on this kernel' and move XREFUSE and the bare stc stubs to it, which needs a census of readers of XREFUSE's AX=1, or keep only the doc half (CF is the sign; AX means something only inside a named family; SPEC 18.4 gets the class/action table). Also say what happens to kern_small's FERR_PROT stubs (kernel.asm:5000-5004), which the 'What moves' list leaves out, and make T5's past-the-end answer the same value as whatever is chosen.

The staged road is right, and nothing like it exists or is in flight: no PROTMODE or mega_kfix anywhere in docs/plans/, SPEC.md or kernel/. But L7's 'affects nothing, +12 .mega' undercounts what has to change in the same diff. (1) tools/os88pkg.py:211-212 rejects any header whose a[15] & 0x3F > STK_CLASS_MAX (4), so a package that sets bit 5 fails to build until the tool masks 0x1F. (2) kernel/sched.inc:2891-2892 carries an %error that pins 'LD_H_CLASS is 6 bits ... masks it with 3Fh'. Both it and instance.inc:2107's 'and bx, 0x3F' change on all kernels, and the SDK prose at apps/os88api.inc:4286-4338 gains a third flag bit. I checked that an old kernel sends bit 5 to the largest class (instance.inc:2114-2116, SCH_NCLASS = 5). (3) The definition of 'clean' has to cover stores through callback ES, not only CS stores. mega_gpw also completes writes through ES = KERNEL_SEG on callbacks, which ABI-BREAK-LIST L3 (line 178) lists separately: Paint x4, os88stik.inc x2. Those are legal under today's callback contract (ES = KERNEL_SEG, CLAUDE.md package-boundary rule). Until the kernel hands a data alias in ES, closing a 'clean' package on that fault would kill legitimate code. The bit's contract must say which fault classes it forbids. (4) gkm-9's 'one-disk 8088/286 product' framing goes against the standing position that no release artefact carries kern_mega's disks (CLAUDE.md memory rule 4; SPEC 20.18 gates mega work to the arm). Present it as an open question for the owner, not as a property of L3. Keeping L3 out of the bundle until The Wire serves kern_mega builds matches ABI-BREAK-LIST.md:178.

The door is sound and fits the other rows: P4 rehearses it first, A4 publishes a level rather than a table end, R9 supplies the AX=1 refusal and T3's rule 4 is strengthened. The vector paragraph has to change, though, because it gets the DOS fit backwards. (1) Leaving the vector out of windowed DOS's exchange set does not protect it. It is what makes it shared. AH=25h writes straight into the live IVT for any vector (apps/dos/dos.asm:4481-4490). dvw_runs banks only 00h, 08h-0Fh and 10h-3Fh (apps/dos/dosw.inc:114-121), so a windowed program that hooks the door vector captures every package's rare call on the whole desktop, not only during its own slices. Virtualising the door vector in DOS's AH=25h and AH=35h paths, in both the windowed and full-screen modes, is therefore a required part of T5, not a later 'designed out'. (2) The vector cannot be anywhere in 60h-80h. os8088's own DOS packet driver takes the first vector in PKT_VEC_LO..PKT_VEC_HI = 60h..80h (apps/dos/dospktabi.inc:22-23) that is NULL or carries no packet-driver signature (apps/dos/dospkt.inc:776-799), so it would overwrite the door. Also exclude 70h-77h (AT slave PIC; the kernel hooks 74h, kernel/mouse.inc:201), 67h (EMS) and 40h-5Fh (BIOS: relocated floppy, disk parameter tables, EGA font, RTC alarm). That leaves 81h-FFh. Name the vector in SPEC.md and add it to the os88intguide anchors. (3) 'Re-enables IF only if the stacked IF was 1' should be written as a push of the stacked FLAGS followed by popf, the form SPEC.md §1's critical-section rule allows, not as a conditional sti. On kern_mega use a TRAP gate, which leaves IF alone and so needs no re-enable at all. That removes part of the +150..+215 clocks there and also answers the open IF question on that kernel. (4) 'Bodies unchanged' holds only for the frame. The shared tails (kernel/kernel.asm:4641-4650, api_rs.tail, also entered by api_rsc and api_rx) become retf 2, so no non-door path may still enter them. P4's cw_ shims must use their own tail or the same retf 2.

The owner has called for this row at the next break (docs/plans/LAST-DROP-BYTES.md 7.13), and the cheap alternative, filling the pad, was refused there for a sound reason. The kern_big figure checks out: FAT_SEG = KERNEL_SEG + KIMG_PARA on every shipped kernel, because ROM_COLD is the default (kernel/kernel.asm:1131-1133, 1795-1804). Two kernels are wrong as written. (a) kern_small: KERNEL_SEG must be one constant on every kernel, because the far-call immediates and ES-on-callback are compiled into packages that run on both (SPEC.md 20.8 rule 4, the T3 row). But kern_small's FAT window is 2 sectors (kernel/kernel.asm:1519; build/smallk/kernel.map FAT_SEG 0x0880, LOW_SEG 0x08C0) against kern_big's 9 (kernel.asm:1565), and 7.13 derives KERNEL_SEG from DSK_FAT_SECS. At a shared 0x01A0, kern_small has 3,584 bytes below its image beyond its own FAT and sector buffer. They must be given fixed-size content, such as its .lowbss stacks and tables with a guard that they fit, or they are a 3.5KB loss on the 64KB-resident machine. Until that is designed, kern_small's -309 is not a saving. (b) kern_mega: LOW_SEG is SS and is used as a selector whose GDT base is i x 128 (kernel/mega.inc:12-15), so the image end still rounds to 128 bytes. Today's 0xC918 rounds to 0xC980, not to 0xCA00, so the saving is about -128, not -232, and about -64 on average. It is 0 if kern_mega keeps its 512-byte rungs (kernel.asm:1170-1171). ABI-BREAK-LIST L1 already said to measure this. Also note that A4's level word sits at KERNEL_SEG:6 and moves with this row.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: -386 kern_big (MEASURED today; 0-511 by build, ~256 average); kern_small ~-309 ONLY if the 7 extra sectors below the shared KERNEL_SEG are given fixed-size content (otherwise up to +3,275); kern_mega ~-128 today (128-byte selector granule; 0-127, ~64 average), 0 if it keeps 512 rungs

verdicts.note: The design fits K17-2, R10 and BR-28, but it loses kern_small's refusal signal. Today OSAPI_WM_ONTIMER and OSAPI_WM_ONDRAG answer CF=1 on kern_small, and the SDK tells packages to 'TEST CF AND HAVE A SECOND PATH' (apps/os88api.inc:3267-3280, 4187-4194). Packages do: apps/1942/1942.asm:56-60 and apps/sheet/sheet.asm:40098. Under R14 the setters vanish and kern_small simply never reads those class slots, so a package arms a timer or a drag that never fires and draws a state it cannot leave. That is the silent-failure shape SPEC.md §47 forbids. R14 must keep an answer, for example: OSAPI_WM_CREATE returns in AL the number of class slots this kernel dispatches (or sets CF/a flag when the class names a slot it cannot dispatch), or OSAPI_WM_TIMER stays the refusal point and a sys flag covers drag. Price that at a few bytes. Two smaller points. Kernel class tables 'in .cold' are read through the one dispatch helper, which must use [api_coldseg] (on mono kern_big `.cold` slides, and that word is in cfx_tab), not COLD_SEG, so price that read. That helper is also where BR-28's W_FLAGS liveness re-test (bugs.md:360-366) belongs, so take the two together.

This conflicts with phase1's WP9 (synth/phase1.md:702-741 and table row 9 at :154). WP9 is the same no-flag-day item, taken now, but it puts `dw osapi_table_end` at 0060:0006 and has `OS88_NEED cell` compare cell offsets. A4 puts a LEVEL there. If WP9 lands as written, every OS88_NEED compiled into packages changes meaning at T5. Pick the level now and change WP9 to match. Also: (1) give the level one source of truth. Today's abilock rule lets an appended cell land with no bump (SPEC.md 20.2.0.1), so t_abilock must also fail an appended cell that does not raise OS88_API_LEVEL, or the level drifts as bumps did before the lock. Share one table with os88wire.py's WIRE_CELL_LEVELS (tools/os88wire.py:114-136) rather than keeping two. (2) Write the address as KERNEL_SEG:6 / [es:6], not as 0060:0006, because L1 moves KERNEL_SEG. (3) Byte 31 is safe on old kernels: inst_set_name_x copies at most 15 bytes (kernel/instance.inc:1242-1256), and the host readers split at NUL (tools/os88disk.py:289, tools/os88drv.py:196). But os88pkg.parse_name refuses any non-NUL byte after the terminator (tools/os88pkg.py:121-124), so it must exempt byte 31 when it stamps the level. Not in flight anywhere: no OS88_NEED or API_LEVEL in the tree.

A cmp of every image proves the binaries, but not the source-scanning gates that match `call\s+OSAPI_X`. After the rewrite they would match nothing and pass: tests/unit/t_movable.py:76-89, t_stkclass.py:67, t_textrules.py:50 (the transparent-text ratchet, whose count 'can only go down', so it would pass while seeing nothing), t_pins.py:144, 201 and 210, and t_toast, t_kdapi, t_megahigh and t_drvclaim. That is the green-row-that-tests-nothing failure docs/WRITING-TESTS.md §1 warns about. The same commit must update each regex and break each one on purpose. Also, 'a cell's KIND stops being source ABI' is already true today: every kind is spelled `call OSAPI_X` (apps/os88api.inc:225, 309, 2222 are all KERNEL_SEG:off %defines, and there are no jmp, dw or push uses of OSAPI_ in apps/ or drivers/). T6's only gain is T5's flip. A cheaper way to get that flip is worth evaluating first: keep `call OSAPI_X` at every site and overload the mnemonic once in os88api.inc (`%imacro call 1`, guarded with %ifid, testing a per-cell kind %define and emitting `int`/`db` for rare cells). That touches no package source, avoids merge churn on the in-flight branches, and keeps every gate's regex valid. Its one risk is whether NASM's warning for a macro that overrides an instruction trips -w+error, so check that first. The renames at the flag day stand as written.
